context.objective: Document how we carry out Accounts Payable, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: So, GPFS, on the management company service line, AP kicks off when the client emails an invoice PDF into Outlook or sends an urgent payment request outside the normal batch cycle. I am the preparer. I confirm the attachment really is an invoice, identify the client and legal entity, and record receipt on the Excel invoice log so nothing gets missed. If the invoice or entity is unclear, it goes back to the client for clarification, then I save the PDF to Box.
What happens after you save the invoice to Box?

Next, iKey vendor, invoice number, date, amount, entity and status into the Excel invoice log, then run the duplicate check on vendor plus invoice number plus amount. A possible duplicate is a hard stop; nothing goes into Entrilia or gets paid until it is resolved and documented, manager or client as needed, no match, I do GL coding, account, accounting class, and the allocation across legal entities using only a current client-approved allocation matrix. Unclear coding gets escalated to the manager or client, never guessed, then I book it in Entrilia.
What happens to the invoice after you book it in Entrilia?

After the Entrilia entry, I compare vendor, invoice number, date, amount, and GL classification in Entrilia back to the PDF and update the invoice log with the Entrilia status and reference. Then I build the approval batch for the weekly, biweekly, or monthly client cycle, compiling invoice PDFs from Box plus the invoice log export, and confirm the batch list and total tie to the log, the manager reviews log, Entrilia record, coding, amounts, duplicate check result, and completeness. I clear review comments, and the batch goes to the client by email or Adobe eSign.
What happens after the approval batch goes to the client?

Client approval is the hard gate. We keep the approval email or Adobe e-sign naming every approved invoice and the total. If the client only partially approves, only the specifically approved items move on, and I record the status of each held or rejected invoice. I add only approved invoices to the payment log: match vendor, amount, entity, and approval support to the package, flag new or changed vendor bank details for the callback and sanctions screening, and hand off to treasury. The treasury initiator and releaser pay through the banking platform under dual control.
What confirms to you that treasury has completed the payment?

Treasury retains the payment confirmation from the banking platform and updates the payment log and invoice log to final status. Failed or pending payments follow the treasury exception path, then I do the close. Invoice log to the box PDFs so every invoice is there once. Entrilia to the PDFs for vendor, invoice number, amount and classification, and paid invoices to payment confirmations. I resolve every difference, mark the invoice paid and closed, manager reviews, and that is the end. Closing schedule, tolerance and status definitions I do not know; those are not confirmed.
What can go wrong in this AP process, and what is the practical consequence?
This capture still has open sections. 15 of 16 are open; the Notes list shows which. You can create a partial draft.

memo_findings.answer: The work processes client invoices for approval and payment.

For GPFS on the management company service line, AP starts when the client emails an invoice PDF into Outlook or sends an urgent payment request outside the normal batch cycle.
Client approval batches follow a weekly, biweekly or monthly client cycle.

Treasury's initiator and releaser pay through the banking platform under dual control after the preparer's handoff.
How held or rejected invoices are ultimately closed remains unspecified.
For paid invoices, closeout includes payment confirmation, reconciliation of the log, PDFs, Entrilia and confirmations, resolution of every difference, marking the invoice paid and closed, and manager review.

The participant is the preparer.
The role accountable for the overall result has not been established.

The participant confirms the attachment is an invoice, identifies the client and legal entity, and records receipt in the Excel invoice log. If the invoice or entity is unclear, the item goes back to the client for clarification; the participant then saves the PDF to Box.
After saving the invoice, the preparer keys vendor, invoice number, date, amount, entity and status into the Excel invoice log and runs a duplicate check on vendor, invoice number and amount.
A possible duplicate is a hard stop: nothing is entered into Entrilia or paid until it is resolved and documented, involving the manager or client as needed.
If there is no duplicate match, the preparer performs GL coding for account and accounting class and allocates across legal entities using a current client-approved allocation matrix. Unclear coding is escalated to the manager or client rather than guessed; the preparer then books it in Entrilia.
After booking in Entrilia, the preparer compares vendor, invoice number, date, amount and GL classification in Entrilia to the PDF, then updates the invoice log with the Entrilia status and reference.
The preparer builds the approval batch for the client's weekly, biweekly or monthly cycle from invoice PDFs in Box and an invoice log export, and ties the batch list and total to the log.
The manager reviews the log, Entrilia record, coding, amounts, duplicate check result and completeness. The preparer clears review comments, and the batch goes to the client by email or Adobe eSign.
Following client approval, only specifically approved items move on if approval is partial; the preparer records each held or rejected invoice's status.
The preparer adds only approved invoices to the payment log, matches vendor, amount, entity and approval support to the package, flags new or changed vendor bank details for callback and sanctions screening, and hands off to Treasury. Treasury's initiator and releaser pay through the banking platform under dual control.
Treasury retains the banking-platform payment confirmation and updates the payment and invoice logs to final status. Failed or pending payments follow the Treasury exception path.
The preparer closes by comparing the invoice log to Box PDFs for one occurrence of every invoice, Entrilia to PDFs for vendor, invoice number, amount and classification, and paid invoices to payment confirmations. The preparer resolves every difference and marks the invoice paid and closed; the manager reviews.

The preparer checks that the attachment really is an invoice and identifies the client and legal entity. If the invoice or entity is unclear, it goes back to the client for clarification.
The preparer checks for duplicates using vendor, invoice number and amount. A possible duplicate blocks Entrilia entry and payment until resolution is documented, with manager or client involvement as needed.
Unclear coding is escalated to the manager or client and is not guessed.
How possible duplicates are investigated, resolved and documented remains unspecified.
The preparer compares the Entrilia vendor, invoice number, date, amount and GL classification against the invoice PDF and ties the approval batch list and total to the invoice log.
The manager reviews the log, Entrilia record, coding, amounts, duplicate check result and completeness; the preparer clears the review comments before the batch goes to the client.
Client approval is a hard gate. The team keeps the approval email or Adobe e-sign naming every approved invoice and the total; if approval is partial, only specifically approved items move on.
The preparer matches vendor, amount, entity and approval support to the package and flags new or changed vendor bank details for callback and sanctions screening. Treasury uses an initiator and releaser under dual control.
Who performs the callback and sanctions screening, how their results are evidenced, and what happens if either fails remain unspecified.
At close the preparer checks the log against Box PDFs for completeness and uniqueness, Entrilia against PDFs for vendor, invoice number, amount and classification, and paid invoices against payment confirmations; the preparer resolves differences and the manager reviews.

An urgent payment request can start AP outside the normal batch cycle.
How urgent requests are handled differently after intake remains unresolved.
The client approval batch cycle can be weekly, biweekly or monthly.

An Excel invoice log is used to record receipt. The invoice PDF is saved to Box after the participant's stated intake actions; Box storage location details are not given.
The Excel invoice log holds vendor, invoice number, date, amount, entity and status. A current client-approved allocation matrix is used for allocations across legal entities.
The approval batch comprises invoice PDFs from Box and an invoice log export; its list and total are checked against the log.
The team retains an approval email or Adobe e-sign naming every approved invoice and the total. The preparer uses a payment log for approved invoices.
Treasury retains banking-platform payment confirmations, which the preparer compares with paid invoices at close.

Specific entity applicability and whether the route varies by client remain unresolved.

Allocation across legal entities uses only a current client-approved allocation matrix.

The method of the client clarification handoff and the condition for returning to the process remain unspecified.

The client approves the batch as a hard gate; after matching and flagging relevant bank details, the preparer hands approved invoices to Treasury, whose initiator and releaser pay under dual control.
AP relies on Treasury's payment confirmation and final log updates for close; failed or pending payments follow the Treasury exception path.

The participant reports that the client emails the invoice PDF into Outlook; receipt is logged in Excel, and the participant saves the PDF to Box. Whether urgent requests use these same tools is not stated.
The preparer keys invoice details into the Excel invoice log and books the coded invoice in Entrilia.
The preparer updates the invoice log with the Entrilia status and reference. The client batch is sent by email or Adobe eSign.
Approval evidence is retained as an email or Adobe e-sign, approved invoices are added to a payment log, and Treasury pays through a banking platform.
Treasury updates both the payment log and invoice log to final status and retains the payment confirmation from the banking platform.
Approval batches are built on a weekly, biweekly or monthly client cycle.

capture.summary: Treasury retains payment confirmations and updates both logs. The preparer reconciles invoices, resolves differences and closes paid invoices, followed by manager review. The closing schedule, tolerance and status definitions are unconfirmed.

connections_out.condition: When the invoice or entity is unclear, the item goes back to the client for clarification; method and return condition are not described.
After manager review and clearance of comments, the approval batch goes to the client by email or Adobe eSign.
Client approval is a hard gate; only specifically approved items advance on partial approval.
After adding approved invoices to the payment log, matching the package and flagging new or changed vendor bank details, the preparer hands off for Treasury payment under dual control.
Treasury retains payment confirmation and updates both logs; the preparer uses payment confirmations in close. Failed or pending payments follow Treasury's exception path.
